Sidebar shows both 'Citas' and 'Contabilidad' entries. /admin/contabilidad loads with summary cards and 'Nuevo cobro' button. /citas/cancelada renders cancellation page. No blocking issues found.

critical_code_review_comments: server.py is 3671 lines - should be split into routers/modules (auth, citas, billing, inbox, chatbot). Violates the 700-line guideline.

book_appointment creates the appointment doc BEFORE attempting Stripe checkout; if Stripe.Price.list or Session.create throws, an orphan pending_payment appointment remains in DB reserving the slot until manually cleaned. Wrap Stripe calls first and only insert after success, or delete the appt on Stripe failure.

book_appointment relies on stripe.Price.list(lookup_keys=['consultation_45min']) but citas/config has a configurable price_amount/currency. The lookup_key ignores the configured price - admin cannot actually change the charged amount from the UI. Consider creating a dynamic price_data line item using config values.
get_available_slots does not validate date format or that date is in the future - could return slots for past dates.

book_appointment does not validate that the chosen date+time actually falls in the configured start/end hours or matches the slot grid - a crafted POST could create appointments outside business hours.
book_appointment stores email lower/stripped but no email format validation (Pydantic EmailStr would be safer).
/api/citas/payment-status/{session_id} is public - session_id is unguessable, but consider signing or requiring the customer email match to prevent enumeration of appointment_id.
stripe.checkout.Session.create is called synchronously (blocking) inside async endpoint - consider await run_in_executor for scale.

BookingPage.js has no client-side validation on required fields (nombres/apellidos/email/telefono/direccion) before enabling btn-to-payment - user can submit blank details and rely on server to bounce.
Missing data-testid on some elements in AdminCitas appointment card actions (delete/review buttons) - would help future automated tests.
